_comment: The tier definitions for the function-calling arm (docs/PROTOCOL.md).
CORRECTED 2026-09-06. This file used to open by saying both paid tiers and the box think here.
One of them did not. The premium tier carried reasoning_effort 'high', which is the
OpenAI-shaped channel, and claude-fable-5 is served on the gateway's Anthropic wire
(wire_protocol 'messages'), where the string reasoning_effort appears nowhere in the backend and
extended thinking travels only as `thinking` inside additionalModelRequestFields -- which that
gateway did not send at all until v1.3.0 (2026-09-06). The parameter was accepted and never
read, so every run of this arm measured a NON-THINKING fable at full price. The recorded
results stand as measurements of that; they are not measurements of a thinking fable, and
fable's cost figures are a lower bound for one. Corroborating evidence from runs already paid
for: across 4,067 rows every Claude model reports reasoning_tokens 0 while every OpenAI and xAI
model reports 92-99% of output as reasoning. reasoning_effort is removed from premium rather
than translated to `thinking`, because translating it would change what this file measures
without saying so; harness/loop.py now refuses the pairing instead of sending it.
Two asymmetries were removed before the arms measured the same thing, and a third was missed:
1. gpt-5.6-terra speaks the Responses API at reasoning_effort 'high'. Bedrock's
OpenAI-compatible endpoint refuses function tools together with any reasoning_effort other
than 'none', and forced to 'none' the tier is a different model: reasoning falls from 80% of
its output tokens to zero, 26% of its steps produce no call at all, and it solves 5 of 15
instead of 9. (Also corrected: the refusal is the provider's, not the gateway's -- the
gateway forwards this route unchanged. The refusal names '/v1/responses'; the gateway serves
it at '/openai/v1/responses'.)
2. The self-hosted deployment starts with --default-chat-template-kwargs={"enable_thinking":
false}, so the box was answering without thinking while terra spent 80% of its output on
reasoning. chat_template_kwargs overrides that per request, so no redeployment is needed.
This deployment has no --reasoning-parser, so the box's thinking arrives as ordinary content
and is billed as ordinary output tokens at $4.12/Mtok -- its expensive side. reasoning_tokens
is therefore 0 for this tier whether thinking is on or off; thinking_chars on each step is
what says it happened.
3. claude-fable-5 was recorded here as needing neither change. It needed one of its own and did
not get it: see the correction at the top. Making this a thinking arm is a new measurement,
not a repair of this one, and it needs `thinking` with a budget below max_tokens -- a budget
equal to it returns reasoning and no answer, billed in full.

self_hosted.rate_basis: measured 2026-08-29 on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, g6e.12xlarge at $15.2174/h, TP=2 x 2 replicas. fresh_in from 18,417 prefill tok/s aggregate at 16 in flight; cache_read from 224,620 tok/s of cached prefill measured the same way, which is 8.2% of a fresh token (benchctl/cached_prefill_rate.py). cache_write priced as fresh input because the engine does the same work to populate a block as to compute it. THIS REPLACES the earlier $10.68 flat rate, whose basis said prefix caching is unsupported on the hybrid attention layers -- that was a missing opt-in flag rather than an architectural limit, so the old rate priced every repeated prompt as recomputed and overstated the box input rate by about 45x.
